title: "Getting started with svyexpo"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Getting started with svyexpo}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(svyexpo)
# Run the model chunks only if INLA is installed and a small model fits here.
has_inla <- requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("sn", quietly = TRUE) &&
  tryCatch({
    s <- svy_simulate(n_side = 3, clusters_per_area = 2,
                      records_per_cluster = 5, seed = 7)
    d <- s$survey
    d$area_id <- s$boundaries$area_id[sf::st_nearest_feature(
      sf::st_as_sf(d, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326), s$boundaries)]
    suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
      svy_fit_bym2(d, y ~ age_months, svy_adjacency(s$boundaries),
                   num.threads = "1:1", silent = 2L)))
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
has_ggplot <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
```

This vignette runs the full workflow on simulated data: a 6 x 6 grid of
areas, 180 clusters displaced as in DHS, and a three-year exposure raster.
With real data, replace `svy_simulate()` with your survey, GPS file, GADM
boundaries and exposure rasters.

```{r}
library(svyexpo)
sim <- svy_simulate()
head(sim$survey)
```

## 1. Ingest

`svy_standardize()` maps your column names to the standard schema. For DHS
recodes, `svy_from_dhs()` does this in one step from the recode and the GPS
dataset.

```{r}
pts <- svy_standardize(
  sim$survey,
  id = "id", cluster = "cluster", lon = "lon", lat = "lat",
  date = "date", weight = "weight", strata = "strata", urban = "urban"
)
```

## 2. Boundaries

With real data, download boundaries with `svy_boundaries("GHA", level = 2)`.
Clusters displaced into the sea or across a border are assigned to the
nearest area within `max_dist` metres.

```{r}
pts <- svy_assign_areas(pts, sim$boundaries)
table(pts$area_match)
```

## 3. Exposure linkage

Buffers are 2 km for urban and 5 km for rural clusters. Each record gets the
exposure layer for its interview year. Here we also average the interview
year and the year before it.

```{r}
buffers <- svy_buffers(pts)
expo <- svy_extract_by_year(buffers, sim$raster, window_years = 2,
                            name = "pm25")
head(expo)
```

`raster` can also be a file path or a Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF URL
(`"/vsicurl/https://..."`). Only the pixels under the buffers are read, and
`cache_file` in `svy_extract()` saves the result so the raster is read once.

## 4. Spatial structure

```{r}
graph <- svy_adjacency(sim$boundaries)
graph
```

## 5. Model

```{r, eval = has_inla}
dat <- merge(sf::st_drop_geometry(pts), expo, by = "id")
dat$pm25_z <- as.numeric(scale(dat$pm25))

fit <- svy_fit_bym2(
  dat, y ~ pm25_z + urban + age_months, graph,
  family = "binomial", svc = "pm25_z"
)
fit
svy_diagnostics(fit)
```

## 6. Outputs

```{r, eval = has_inla}
area <- svy_area_effects(fit, exponentiate = TRUE)
slopes <- svy_svc_effects(fit, "pm25_z", exponentiate = TRUE)
head(slopes)
```

```{r, eval = has_inla && has_ggplot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
svy_map(slopes, sim$boundaries, fill = "mean",
        title = "Odds ratio per SD of PM2.5")
svy_map(slopes, sim$boundaries, fill = "prob_exceed",
        title = "P(odds ratio > 1)")
```
